outcome: maternal emotional experiences (stress, fear, shock, guilt, denial, difficulty accepting delivery)
factors improving maternal experience (high-quality healthcare, careful monitoring, peer and social support, empathetic healthcare providers)
cohort: The study included five mothers in the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia who had premature infants who were under one year old at the time of data collection.
finding: Mothers frequently experience stress, fear, shock, guilt, denial, and difficulty accepting premature delivery, while high-quality healthcare, careful monitoring, and strong support systems significantly improve their experience.
cross-section timing: Data collected when infants were under one year old.
